judgements.reason: DT needs Roth, the subspace theorem, Baker–Matveev bounds, effective Thue–Mahler equations and E/G-function transcendence, but beyond Mathlib's heights, Siegel lemma and Liouville it imports only Minkowski's second theorem and LLL. IHG needs Chenevier determinants, generalized matrix algebras, derived Hecke nilpotence and the DKSW Ribet theorem stacked on smooth representations, the Satake isomorphism and Bruhat–Tits buildings, parahoric group schemes and integral dual groups (RG2), plus Chebotarev density: a comparable amount in a deeper stack.

AS needs algebraic spaces and stacks with Hilbert/Picard representability and Artin's criteria (R09.1–R09.6), p-divisible, Dieudonné, Breuil–Kisin and Grothendieck–Messing theory with period rings and perfectoid basics, and complex GAGA (C0–C4) before its duals, Serre–Tate and Siegel family. IHG's polynomial-law determinants, GMAs, DKSW theorem and imported Satake/Bruhat–Tits theory form a much smaller algebraic stack.

AS must build algebraic spaces, stacks, coarse spaces and Artin representability, formal geometry, Dieudonné/Breuil–Kisin/Grothendieck–Messing theory and complex-analytic GAGA before its duals, polarizations, Serre–Tate and uniformization. DV's stack is deeper but narrower — diamonds, v-descent and spatial diamonds (D1–D6) on perfectoid limits (P4–P6), adic étale approximation (A2–A4) and the prismatic perfectoidization theorem (Q0–Q4, PR.0–PR.2) — and it shares D0, P0–P3 and E0–E5 with AS.

PerfectoidSpaces already imports D0–D4 and the prismatic Q4 stack, so its closure contains nearly all of DV's; beyond that it needs tilde-limits and towers, finite quotients with closed perfectoidization and torsor descent (P7–P9) and rigid geometry (AdicSpacesPartII R0–R3, R5). DV adds only spatial diamonds (D5), Spd of analytic adic spaces (D6) and the A4 presentations.

AC's closure contains P0–P6, D0–D6 and the prismatic stack and adds étale cohomology of diamonds (C0–C9), Huber's adic étale cohomology (H0–H5), scheme étale duality (EDC.0–EDC.4), the diamond six operations (S0–S5) and its own adic coefficients, Nagata compactification and de Jong alterations. PerfectoidSpaces adds only P7–P9 and AdicSpacesPartII.

Through K3BlochGroups V.5 and HabiroNahmSeries HB.9, AQT imports the norm-residue theorem and motivic spectral sequence (M.4–M.7), Quillen and Borel K-theory, THH/TC local K-theory and p-adic regulators, on top of its own Kirby calculus, Reshetikhin–Turaev and Habiro invariants, hyperbolic Bloch regulators and state integrals. AC's missing diamond six-functor stack with ECD §§26–27, Nagata compactification and alterations is clearly smaller.

DWP needs scheme étale foundations and duality (EDC.0–EDC.4), Lefschetz pencils and vanishing cycles (LPV), abelian-scheme duals (A1–A3, A6) and then Weil I/II with hard Lefschetz. AQT needs the whole arithmetic K-theory stack (norm-residue theorem, Quillen and Borel K-theory, THH/TC, HabiroNumberFields) plus Kirby calculus, quantum-group invariants, Habiro's unified invariant and hyperbolic Bloch regulators, far more.

DSO's closure already contains DWP's foundations (scheme étale theory, EDC.0–EDC.4, LPV.0–LPV.2, A1–A3, R09.1–R09.4) and adds perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Huber's and diamond étale cohomology (P0–P6, D0–D6, H0–H5, C0–C9), the prismatic Q4 stack and the six operations. DWP adds only Weil I/II, hard Lefschetz, the pencil and monodromy layers LPV.3–LPV.7 and A6.

HNF imports the norm-residue theorem with motivic homotopy, Rost motives and the motivic spectral sequence (M.1–M.7), Quillen's K-theory, Suslin's K3 theorem, Borel's stable cohomology with reduction theory, and local K-theory via THH/TC (L.1–L.6, RT.1–RT.4) before its Habiro modules. DSO's diamond stack (ECD étale cohomology and six operations, Huber's adic étale cohomology, SGA4-level duality, perfectoid and prismatic inputs, algebraic stacks) is equally deep but somewhat smaller.

VBI adds the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve and its diamond, rigid geometry, bundle classification and Banach–Colmez spaces to the diamond stack through S0–S5 (C0–C9, H0–H4, EDC, perfectoid, prismatic). HNF's imported norm-residue theorem, motivic cohomology and étale K-theory, Quillen and Borel K-theory, THH/TC local K-theory and p-adic regulators amount to somewhat more.

PAI's closure contains all but a dozen of VBI's layers (diamonds, six operations, étale cohomology of diamonds, perfectoid spaces, most of the Fargues–Fontaine curve) and adds Weil II, endoscopic transfer with the fundamental lemma, Shimura and Igusa varieties with Caraiani–Scholze vanishing, automorphic Galois representations and derived patching. VBI adds only its own isocrystal, bundle and Banach–Colmez layers.

RTM needs spectra, THH/TC and trace comparisons, q-Hodge and cyclonic spectra, refined localizing invariants and BMS2 with prismatic, A_inf and Habiro-ring inputs, about 75 layers. PAI's closure of about 355 layers spans étale and diamond cohomology, Weil II, Shimura and Igusa varieties, the trace formula and fundamental lemma, automorphic Galois representations and patching.

SVBT needs Wiles's and Kurihara's main conjectures with DKSW integral Brumer–Stark, modular-curve moduli, Deligne–Ribet p-adic zeta functions, Tate's K_2 theorems, the norm-residue theorem, Quillen–Borel K-theory, Borel regulators and polylogarithms, and it even contains RT.1–RT.4. RTM's own trace, q-Hodge, refined-invariant and BMS2 layers with their Habiro and prismatic imports are much less.

SVBT's arithmetic stack (Iwasawa main conjectures and integral Brumer–Stark, modular curves, K_2, K_3 and higher K-theory with the norm-residue theorem, Borel regulators, p-adic L-functions) is about 210 layers. AC's missing theory is the diamond six-functor stack with Huber and ECD étale cohomology, SGA4-level duality, alterations and Nagata compactification, about 100 layers.

DV needs perfectoid spaces P0–P6, adic étale geometry, the prismatic perfectoidization theorem and ∞-categorical sheaf foundations before diamonds and v-descent. DT's Roth, subspace theorem, Baker bounds and E/G-functions sit directly on Mathlib's heights, Siegel lemma and Liouville with only Minkowski's second theorem and LLL imported.

SVBT's missing theory is the arithmetic K-theory and Iwasawa stack (norm residue, Quillen–Borel K-theory, main conjectures, modular curves, regulators). PAI's much larger closure (about 355 layers against 210) contains étale, perverse and diamond cohomology, Weil II, perfectoid Shimura and Igusa varieties, endoscopic transfer with the fundamental lemma, the trace formula, automorphic Galois representations and patching.

PS needs almost mathematics, tilting, sheafiness, almost purity, limits and towers, with imported prismatic cohomology up to perfectoidization, D0–D4, adic étale and rigid geometry and ∞-categorical sheaves (about 50 layers). IHG's determinants, GMAs, DKSW theorem and imported Satake/Bruhat–Tits theory (about 20 layers) are a smaller, shallower stack.

DWP contains AS's core (A1–A3, A6 with R09.1–R09.4) and stacks on it scheme étale foundations and duality (EDC.0–EDC.4), vanishing cycles, Lefschetz pencils and Kazhdan–Margulis monodromy (LPV), then Weil I/II and hard Lefschetz. AS instead needs wide but shallower side branches — Serre–Tate via Dieudonné, Breuil–Kisin and Grothendieck–Messing, complex GAGA for uniformization, Artin representability and formal geometry — so the amounts are close and DWP's taller tower decides.

VBI needs the diamond stack through S0–S5 (diamond étale cohomology, Huber's adic étale cohomology, EDC and scheme étale theory, perfectoid and prismatic inputs, algebraic stacks) plus the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve, rigid geometry and bundle classification. RTM needs spectra, THH/TC, Bott periodicity, Wagner's cyclonic q-Hodge theory, Efimov's refined invariants and BMS2 with A_inf, prismatic and Habiro inputs: comparable, but VBI's stack is larger and much deeper.

AQT imports all of HabiroNumberFields' K-theory (norm residue, motivic cohomology, Quillen and Borel K-theory, THH/TC, p-adic regulators) and adds Kirby calculus, ribbon-category and Reshetikhin–Turaev invariants, Habiro's unified invariant and hyperbolic Bloch regulators. DSO's diamond six-functor stack is clearly smaller.

AC adds ECD §§26–27, Nagata compactification and de Jong alterations with cohomological descent to the diamond stack (diamond and Huber étale cohomology, EDC and scheme étale theory, perfectoid, prismatic, six operations). HNF's imported norm-residue theorem, motivic spectral sequence, étale K-theory, Quillen and Borel K-theory, THH/TC local K-theory and p-adic regulators amount to somewhat more.

AS needs algebraic spaces and stacks with Artin representability, p-divisible group and Grothendieck–Messing theory, complex GAGA and its own duals, polarizations and Serre–Tate, about 50 layers. DT's approximation and transcendence theorems sit on Mathlib's heights, Siegel lemma and Liouville with only Minkowski's second theorem and LLL imported.

SVBT needs the arithmetic stack of Iwasawa main conjectures, integral Brumer–Stark, modular curves, K_2 and higher K-theory with the norm-residue theorem, Borel regulators and p-adic L-functions, about 210 layers. VBI's diamond stack with Fargues–Fontaine bundles and Banach–Colmez spaces, about 120 layers, is smaller.

PAI's closure contains every layer DV needs (perfectoid, prismatic, D0–D6) and adds the diamond six operations, Weil II, Shimura and Igusa varieties, the fundamental lemma, automorphic Galois representations and patching. DV's diamonds and v-stacks are a small part of it.
